_comment: The counted-set test, carried over from simulate-outcome-classification.json when the rule
moved out of the ingest pipeline and into the dashboard's own query.
WHY IT HAD TO BE CARRIED OVER RATHER THAN DROPPED. Three of these templates -- an input-schema
rejection, an output-schema rejection and an unhandled transform fault -- do not fire in normal
traffic. They are also the three an operator most needs to see. A live measurement cannot cover
them, so without this fixture the rule would be verified only on the six templates that happen
to fire, which is exactly the defect section 4 of the spec exists to record.
The old form was a body for _ingest/pipeline/_simulate. There is no pipeline any more, so these
are indexed into a scratch index and the rule is run against them as a query.
TWO DIFFERENCES FROM THE OLD FIXTURE, both forced by the new rule:
1. Every document carries resource.attributes.service.name. The old rule keyed on scope.name
and never looked at the service; the new one asks whether the emitter is the orchestrator.
2. There is a thirteenth document. ProcessDispatchHandler now emits the terminal step's own
Completed outcome, which did not exist when the first twelve were written, and it is the
document that makes the orchestrator's copy redundant.
THE VERDICT THAT MOVED: doc 7, the orchestrator's terminal-step Completed. The old rule counted
it -- it was the entire reason the old rule needed a second clause. The new rule does not,
because doc 13 now reports the exporter's success through its no-data branch
(ProcessedDataHandler's "branch completed in {ElapsedMs}ms"). Its EntryId is Guid.Empty and
therefore absent, and check 5 accepts it as a by-design skip for kafka-exporter.

docs.why: the ordinary success of a step that hands on output
RARE IN TRAFFIC - an output-schema rejection; one of the three this fixture exists for

the author reported the step failed: {Reason}

docs.why: a policy rejection, and the processor is always its witness - never the orchestrator
RARE IN TRAFFIC - an unhandled transform fault; one of the three this fixture exists for

attributes.{OriginalFormat}: the transform faulted — reporting the step failed

docs.why: THE VERDICT THAT MOVED. The old rule counted this and needed a whole second clause to do it. Doc 13 now carries the same outcome from the processor side, so counting this one as well would double it

attributes.{OriginalFormat}: the terminal step completed with {Result} — no successor accepts it, the run ends here

docs.why: a restatement of doc 5 - the processor already reported the cancellation for the same step and lineage

attributes.{OriginalFormat}: the terminal step completed with {Result} — no successor accepts it, the run ends here

docs.why: restates an outcome the processor side already emitted for the same step
restates a failure the processor already reported, while advancing successors that accept it

attributes.{OriginalFormat}: advancing {SuccessorCount} successor(s) on a {Result} step — their entry conditions accept it

docs.why: a counted record is counted on its Result and its emitter, never on whether its ids resolve to anything
a future framework line under a processor service that carries no Result - the rule must not sweep it in

attributes.{OriginalFormat}: a record with no Result at all

docs.why: The sink's own success after 2026-09-29: kafka-exporter reports Completed through a branch with no data, so the record comes from the post handler like every other step. Its EntryId is Guid.Empty, which ExecutionLogScope omits, so check 5 accepts it as a skip for this processor

NEW 2026-09-26. A refusal, not an outcome: GatedQueueConsumer rejected the delivery without requeue and the broker dead-lettered it, so the step reported nothing at all. It carries WorkflowId, StepId and ProcessorId - lifted off the delivery's own x-skp-* headers, because the handler's scope was already disposed by the unwinding exception - and that is exactly why it belongs here: it looks as joinable as an outcome and has no Result, so a rule keyed on the ids rather than on Result would count thrown-away work as completed work

attributes.{OriginalFormat}: refusing message of type {Type} on {Queue} — parked

docs.why: NEW 2026-09-26. The other half of the same catch block: the channel died before the broker heard the rejection, so the message is REDELIVERED rather than dead-lettered and there is nothing in a dead-letter queue to recover. One code branch, one metric bucket and one severity with doc 14 - the template is the only thing telling them apart, which is why the refusal table splits them with a phrase match on body.text - match_only_text, so it answers a phrase query, unlike the keyword attributes.* fields

attributes.{OriginalFormat}: refusing message of type {Type} on {Queue} — NOT parked: the channel was gone before the broker was told, so it will be redelivered rather than dead-lettered
